title: Intraoperative STN/thalamic DBS-lead LFP with subgaleal sensorimotor strips during a stop-signal task (Diesburg, Greenlee & Wessel, 2021)
description: Intraoperative local field potential recordings from deep brain stimulation leads in the subthalamic nucleus or ventral intermediate thalamus, together with subgaleal strip electrodes over sensorimotor cortex. Data were collected from 23 patients undergoing DBS surgery while they performed an auditory stop-signal task and a go-only localizer. The dataset supports analysis of cortico-subcortical beta burst dynamics underlying movement cancellation, where subcortical beta bursts on successful stop trials are followed shortly by sensorimotor cortical beta bursts.
methods_description: Recordings were acquired during DBS surgery at the University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics (April 2018 to March 2020) using a TDT system with an RA16PA Medusa preamplifier and RA16LI headstage, with a hardware low-pass at 7.5 kHz. Medtronic 3387 leads were placed in the STN or VIM, with 4-, 6- or 8-contact subgaleal strips over sensorimotor cortex. Sampling rates were 2000 or 24000 Hz, and task triggers were recorded as TTL pulses on analog input channels.
